title: H3052 (122nd General Assembly): Jacob Hall School Protection Act

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, South Carolina); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Carolina text (Introduced, 2016-12-15; official copy, https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess122_2017-2018/prever/3052_20161215.htm (LegiScan doc 1439455))
provenance.note: Introduced 2016-12-15 ('Jacob Hall School Protection Act'). Private schools are exempt but may opt in (Section 59-63-690). Passage vote: none listed; introduced text only.

operative_text:
Section 1 (new Section 59-63-620): A public school concealed weapons permit (PSCWP) is a specialized permit authorized by this article which enables a person to possess a concealed weapon on public school property, notwithstanding another provision of law, for the purpose of confronting a live shooter or an imminent threat of a live shooter in his vicinity on school property.
Section 1 (new Section 59-63-630): (A) The South Carolina Law Enforcement Division shall provide a PSCWP for the limited purposes provided in this article.
Section 1 (new Section 59-63-630): (B) A determination of whether the policy of a particular school is to allow its employees to obtain a PSCWP is within the exclusive jurisdiction of the principal of the school.
Section 1 (new Section 59-63-630): (D) A PSCWP is valid for five years and may be renewed through a process developed by SLED.
Section 1 (new Section 59-63-630): (F)(2) A PSCWP holder shall carry his concealed weapon properly holstered on his person at all times on school grounds, if he brings the weapon onto the school grounds.
Section 1 (new Section 59-63-640): SLED shall approve at least three concealed carry holsters and their vendors and provide a list of these approved holsters and vendors to a PSCWP holder.
Section 1 (new Section 59-63-670): (A) A PSCWP holder may carry his weapon any place that any other concealed weapons permit holder may carry.
Section 1 (new Section 59-63-680): The identities of PSCWP holders may not be made available to the public and are exempt from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act, notwithstanding another provision of law.
